figures: 1. Figure 1: Overview of the CUSUM-calibrated rollback controller. Both Or-ϵ (top pathway) and CUSUM-ϵ (bottom pathway) use the same probe loss measurement and innovation signal, but differ in their decision rules: Or-ϵ triggers rollback when innovation exceeds threshold ϵ, while CUSUM-ϵ accumulates evidence via statistic St and triggers when St > h. Both are calibrated to the same nominal rollback rate p0 = 0.2%. The FIR partial reset (St ← h/2 after rollback) addresses the reset blind spot in standard CUSUM.
results_section: 1. Both controllers dramatically reduce perturbation damage compared to no controller (>80% reduction in peak excess loss).
2. For step perturbation, Or-ϵ achieves 1.88× lower peak excess loss
3. For step perturbation, Or-ϵ achieves 1.47× lower excess AUC
4. For ramp perturbation, similar gaps persist (1.77× lower peak excess loss).
5. For ramp perturbation, similar gaps persist (1.85× lower excess AUC).
6. CUSUM-ϵ does achieve 58% fewer false rollbacks outside the perturbation window
7. When perturbations cause large innovation spikes (>5σ above baseline), Or-ϵ detects immediately while CUSUM-ϵ needs 2–3 steps to accumulate sufficient evidence
8. approximately 3 steps were needed to re-accumulate evidence during ongoing perturbation.
9. FIR partial reset (St ← h/2) allows re-triggering within 1–2 anomalous steps.
10. peak excess loss decreases by 35–36% for both perturbation types
